articles.title: Ohio State Faces Michigan Without Postseason Implications
articles.summary: The Buckeyes' chances of making the College Football Playoff or reaching the Big Ten championship game are slim to none.
articles.content: Ohio State's season may be all but over, but there's still a glimmer of hope for the Buckeyes - beating Michigan would salvage their pride and give them bragging rights on their archrivals. This is the first time in Ryan Day's era that Ohio State faces Michigan without any real postseason implications hanging in the balance. The team will need to dig deep and channel their disappointment into a win against the one opponent that matters most on their schedule. The Buckeyes' chances of making the College Football Playoff or reaching the Big Ten championship game are slim to none, barring an extraordinary set of circumstances. All that's left is potential bragging rights, but beating Michigan would be a significant accomplishment in itself. Ohio State could save face in what has been a disappointing season by defeating their rivals for the second year running - something they haven't achieved since the 2010s. Michigan's offense has been clicking lately, with freshman running back Savion Hiter playing a key role. He rushed for 104 yards on 26 carries last week against UCLA, his second consecutive 100-yard game. According to Pro Football Focus, Hiter has picked up 194 of his 212 rushing yards after contact over the past two games - a testament to his bruising style. Stopping Hiter and Michigan's running game will be crucial for Ohio State if they want to emerge victorious. With their season hanging in the balance, the Buckeyes will need all their energy and determination to channel their disappointment into a win against their archrivals. The Ohio State offense will need to improve its tackling skills if they hope to contain Michigan's Jamal Rule, who has already given them trouble in their previous loss against Nebraska. Michigan's passing game is also a key area for the Buckeyes to target, with an average of the fewest yards per game among Power 4 teams putting pressure on their offense. For Ohio State to emerge victorious, they will need to win the turnover battle - a challenge that has proven difficult in recent games, as both teams have struggled with mistakes in conference play. Michigan's defense excelled in forcing turnovers against UCLA, including a crucial recovered fumble by quarterback Ty Dieffenbach that set up their lone touchdown. Ohio State's offense will need to navigate a formidable defensive front when facing Michigan. A clean pocket is essential for quarterback Julian Sayin to operate effectively and control the line of scrimmage, which in turn allows the running game to thrive. Michigan's defense has been one of the most impressive units in the country, allowing less than 3 yards per carry to opponents this season. The Buckeyes' own running game will have to contend with Utah transfer defensive end John Henry Daley, who has anchored Michigan's pass rush and adds an extra layer of complexity. Protecting freshman quarterback Luke Fahey will be a top priority for the Buckeyes, as they face off against one of the best defensive fronts in the country. articles.title: Bacteria Colonies Change Shape Under Oxygen Scarcity
articles.summary: Researchers from the University of Cologne's Institute for Biological Physics have investigated how Neisseria gonorrhoeae bacteria colonies change shape and structure over time.
articles.content: Bacteria form colonies to shield themselves from harm, but scientists have long been puzzled by how these colonies change shape and structure over time. Researchers from several institutions, including the University of Cologne's Institute for Biological Physics, have investigated this phenomenon in Neisseria gonorrhoeae, a bacterium responsible for causing gonorrhea. Their study reveals that when oxygen becomes scarce within a colony, the bacteria rapidly consume what little oxygen is available and respond by reducing their attraction to one another. This reduction in attractive forces leads to a loss of shape stability, causing the bacteria at the center of the colony to flow towards the surface where oxygen levels are higher. As a result, the colony undergoes a transformation known as global eversion and dissemination, with bacteria moving from the interior outwards. The study's findings have significant implications for research into antibiotic tolerance in bacteria, which can form colonies that protect them from treatment by antibiotics and even the immune system. Bacteria have evolved various strategies to adapt to their environment, and forming colonies is a common tactic that allows them to thrive in diverse conditions. When resources are plentiful, these microorganisms can live as solitary entities, but under scarcity they often group together to form spatially structured communities. This phenomenon bears striking similarities to embryonic development, where cells differentiate into distinct physiological states based on their local environment. The study focused on Neisseria gonorrhoeae, a bacterium that exhibits unique behavior in response to oxygen deprivation. When the colony's center lacks sufficient oxygen, the cells slow down production of type 4 pili, molecular appendages that enable bacteria to attach themselves to surfaces. As neighboring cells interact through these pili, the force of attraction at the colony's surface becomes stronger compared to its center. The researchers faced significant challenges in characterizing the attractive interactions within living colonies. According to Dr. Stephan Wimmi, a lead author on the study, "It was a particularly challenging experiment to characterize these attractive interactions within the living colonies." Despite these difficulties, the team successfully shed light on the intricate mechanisms governing bacterial colony formation. The findings of this research have significant implications for understanding how bacteria develop resistance to antibiotics and evade the immune system. By studying the behavior of Neisseria gonorrhoeae in response to oxygen scarcity, scientists can gain valuable insights into the complex interactions between microorganisms and their environment. The researchers at the Institute for Biological Physics have made a groundbreaking discovery about how bacterial colonies respond to low oxygen levels. This phenomenon was first observed under the microscope by professor Berenike Maier's team when they noticed that the colony was turning itself inside out in response to oxygen scarcity. According to Maier, it was an impressive sight and one that could not be explained by conventional methods of microbiological study. The researchers have since used theoretical modeling to understand this complex process. The bacteria responsible for gonorrhea, Neisseria gonorrhoeae, are likely to experience periods of low oxygen levels during their infection cycle. This has significant implications for the development of new treatments and therapies for the disease. By studying how these bacteria adapt to low oxygen conditions, scientists may be able to identify potential weaknesses in the bacterial defenses. The research team is also investigating how bacteria control their physical interactions with one another. To achieve this, they are combining biophysical methods with microbiological techniques to manipulate the forces of interaction between individual cells. This approach has allowed them to measure the forces at play and gain a deeper understanding of the complex dynamics involved. Maier's explanation for the colony's behavior in response to low oxygen levels is that the bacteria reduce their growth and metabolism, essentially "going to sleep" to protect themselves from antibiotics. However, this protective strategy comes with significant costs, including reduced access to nutrients and oxygen. The researchers are now seeking to understand how bacteria balance protection against growth restriction as a community. As oxygen levels drop, bacterial colonies undergo a remarkable transformation. They turn themselves inside out by expelling their outer layer, releasing it into the surrounding environment. This process is driven by two key factors: differential active adhesion and capillary instability. The former allows bacteria to stick to surfaces in a way that's both strong and weak at the same time, while the latter creates an unstable situation where the colony's outer layer becomes detached. articles.title: Global Canopy Atlas Unveiled by University Researchers
articles.summary: A new atlas has been unveiled by an international team of researchers led by the University of Bristol in the UK, providing high-resolution 3D maps of forests and savannas worldwide.
articles.content: A groundbreaking new atlas has been unveiled by an international team of researchers led by the University of Bristol in the UK. The Global Canopy Atlas is a comprehensive collection of high-resolution 3D maps of forests, woodlands, and savannas from around the world. The study, published in Nature Ecology and Evolution, offers a unique and consistent view of the planet's woody ecosystems. This achievement has far-reaching implications for research on forest carbon stocks and biodiversity conservation efforts. It also provides new opportunities for scientists to map these delicate ecosystems. More than 100 institutions worldwide were involved in this ambitious five-year project, which brings together thousands of airborne LiDAR surveys from across the globe. LiDAR technology uses laser-scanning to create detailed 3D maps of vegetation and terrain over vast areas. The Global Canopy Atlas offers a vital resource for scientists seeking to understand the complex relationships between forest canopies and their role in regulating life on Earth. According to Tommaso Jucker, co-lead study author and professor of forest ecology and global change at the University of Bristol, The aerial structure of forests plays a vital role in regulating life on Earth. The new forest atlas is set to revolutionize the way researchers, policymakers, and practitioners work together to conserve and manage forests worldwide. The atlas brings together nearly 3,500 high-resolution aerial LiDAR surveys conducted from various aircraft and drones over 56 countries and 224 distinct ecological regions. Spanning a vast area of over 5.5 million hectares (13.6 million acres), the data encompasses diverse forest types, including dense tropical rainforests and sparse dry woodlands. A standard methodology was used to ensure consistency in quality and comparability across all surveys, providing researchers with high-resolution 3D maps of both canopy height and terrain elevation for each survey. This standardized approach is crucial for making informed decisions about forest management and conservation efforts. By consolidating thousands of fragmented data sets into a single global resource, the atlas offers a unique snapshot of ecological dynamics in these regions, allowing for better understanding of how woody ecosystems function and respond to disturbances that impact Earth's climate stability. The new atlas provides a comprehensive platform for researchers and conservation organizations to access and utilize LiDAR data from nearly 3,500 laser surveys conducted across 56 countries. Users can explore the interactive map to identify where, when, and by whom data have been collected worldwide, facilitating easy access and utilization of this valuable resource. This online tool is a result of collaboration between the European Space Agency and the International Institute for Applied Systems Analysis, highlighting the importance of international partnerships in advancing ecological research. The atlas's capabilities extend beyond mere data storage, allowing ecologists to analyze ecosystem structure and dynamics across varying landscapes and continents. This information can be used to understand how these dynamics shape biodiversity, providing valuable insights for conservation efforts. By leveraging this knowledge, conservation organizations can refine their strategies for monitoring priority habitats and assessing the effectiveness of restoration interventions. The Global Canopy Atlas is poised to play a significant role in validating and calibrating next-generation satellite monitoring systems, including those used by governments, policymakers, and environmental agencies. As part of this effort, the European Space Agency's BIOMASS mission aims to map global forest carbon stocks, with the atlas serving as a critical resource for tracking progress and informing policy decisions. The Global Canopy Atlas brings together an unprecedented 3,500 laser surveys to create a comprehensive map of forests across 56 countries worldwide. This extensive dataset offers researchers and policymakers a valuable tool for tracking forest health and informing conservation efforts. With the European Space Agency's BIOMASS mission aiming to map global forest carbon stocks, this atlas serves as a critical resource for monitoring progress and guiding policy decisions. The atlas provides analysis-ready maps of 3D structure for the world's woody ecosystems, offering insights into forest composition, density, and biomass distribution. articles.title: UK Government Launches Emergency Preparedness Campaign
articles.summary: The UK government has launched a campaign advising households to stock up on essential supplies in case of emergencies.
articles.content: The UK government's recent "Be Ready campaign has caught many off guard, advising households to stock up on essential supplies in case of emergencies. Brian, a Scottish engineer, is part of this new wave of preparedness. He remembers the 2010 winter that brought the country to its knees, with heavy snowfall crippling major roads and leaving families struggling to access basic necessities. In the aftermath of that event, Brian decided he wouldn't be caught off guard again. He began building a store of non-perishable food and other essential supplies, ready for any unexpected shortages or disruptions. It's very hard to look your kids in the eye when you're looking at a relatively empty cupboard, he says candidly about his decision to prepare for emergencies. Brian now shares his expertise with others through online tutorials on YouTube, where he goes by the handle Scottishprepper73. His stash is so comprehensive that he believes his family could survive for an entire year without external help. As news of the government's campaign spreads, British preppers are finding themselves thrust into the spotlight, despite operating on the fringes until now. The heightened awareness of government campaigns has had a profound impact on people's perception of prepping. It's not just the fringe anymore; ordinary individuals are now embracing the idea of building household resilience. This shift can be attributed to the breaking down of normalcy bias, where people begin to see the value in preparing for unexpected events. Preppers like Glyn Smith have observed a significant increase in interest from normal person preppers. These individuals aren't interested in apocalyptic scenarios or advanced survival skills; they simply want to ensure their families are equipped to handle everyday challenges. As a result, prepper communities are now seeing an influx of people who were previously uninterested. The founder of the UK Survival Network has also reported a surge in interest among ordinary citizens. These aren't lone survivalists or extreme enthusiasts; instead, it's mums, dads, couples, and retirees who want to be prepared for life's uncertainties. This shift is significant, as it shows that prepping is no longer seen as an eccentric pursuit. However, not everyone is welcoming of the growing interest in prepping. Some people respond with aggression when confronted with the idea of preparing for potential disasters. Preppers have reported receiving death threats and hostile messages from individuals who are skeptical or dismissive of their efforts. The pushback against prepping is multifaceted, ranging from accusations of fearmongering to criticism that it's a waste of time and money. Some people feel that the government should provide for them instead of relying on individual preparedness. Others complain about the cost of prepping, feeling that it's an unaffordable luxury. Despite these criticisms, preppers are trying to change the public's perception of their community. They're not the eccentric survivalists often portrayed in the media; rather, they're ordinary people who want to be prepared for everyday challenges like storms and floods. By focusing on practical, achievable goals, preppers aim to make their efforts seem more relatable and accessible to a wider audience. A single incident like a burst water pipe or power outage can easily disrupt daily life in localized areas. This is not just hypothetical; supermarkets across Europe were recently targeted by hackers in an attack that has been attributed to Iran. The aftermath of such incidents would be predictable: supermarket shelves might go bare, taps run dry, and the lights could flicker out. Ana, a prepper from south Wales, concurs on this point. She emphasizes that disruptions like these can have far-reaching consequences for basic necessities. It's going to affect your food supply in supermarkets, your water, and your electricity, she warns. Ana's own experiences with food preservation and long-term storage were sparked by her early life growing up on a farm where she learned the value of self-sufficiency. She has continued these habits throughout her life. Her YouTube channel initially focused on cooking from scratch, but after realizing most people lacked basic knowledge about preserving food for extended periods, she shifted gears to prepper content. Brian's home in Scotland is equipped with a range of tech-heavy setup features that would put many preppers' off-grid plans to shame. For him, it's not about abandoning modern conveniences, but rather about being prepared for the worst. A significant portion of Brian's water storage capacity consists of 165 gallons of fresh water, which he refreshes every six months, ensuring a steady supply in case of emergencies. He has no need for bottled water, as he notes that Scotland has never struggled with water scarcity. Unlike many preppers who plan to go off the grid if power and internet fail, Brian has taken a different approach. His house is fitted with solar panels, an air source heat pump provides heating, and a generator serves as backup power. He also has a diesel-powered heater for added security. Brian's tech-heavy setup extends beyond his home's infrastructure, with him relying on Starlink for internet access and running two mesh networking systems as a precautionary measure. In the event that these fail, he has high-frequency radio as an ultimate fallback to stay connected. In preparation for prolonged power outages, Brian has stockpiled essential items in his shed. His collection includes flashlights, lanterns, candles, radios, walkie-talkies, and even a night-vision headset, ensuring that life doesn't have to become unbearable in the absence of electricity. Brian's approach stands in contrast to many US preppers who plan to leave their homes behind and live off the grid. As Chappell notes, British preppers tend to stay at home due to the lack of vast wilderness areas for them to escape to. Preppers in the UK often face challenges when it comes to stocking up on essential supplies due to space constraints in urban areas. For some, this means prioritizing certain items over others, such as nappies for short-term emergencies. While prepping is typically seen as a solo activity, many British preppers are part of close-knit communities that rely on one another in times of crisis. This communal approach is rooted in the understanding that resources and expertise can be shared more effectively when neighbors work together. Secrecy often surrounds prepping activities in the UK, with some individuals keeping their stockpiles hidden from prying eyes due to concerns about becoming targets for looters or opportunists. However, this approach may not always be feasible, especially for those living in densely populated urban areas. In contrast, others believe that community engagement can help foster trust and cooperation during emergencies. By setting up neighborhood WhatsApp groups and offering small favors to neighbors, preppers can establish a foundation for collaboration when it matters most. This idea is based on the notion that people tend to come together rather than turn on each other in times of crisis, drawing inspiration from historical events such as the Blitz. While some may view this perspective as overly optimistic, others see it as a necessary mindset shift. In emergency scenarios, pooling resources and knowledge can be more effective than going it alone, as seen in situations where neighbors have worked together to overcome challenges. However, not everyone shares this view, with some expressing concerns that the lack of information during power outages could lead to panic and poor decision-making. As the UK prepares for potential power outages, individuals are taking steps to ensure their safety and well-being. For some, this means having a plan in place for emergency situations, such as bugging out to a safe location if necessary. Prepping has become a hobby for many, with meet-ups and workshops providing opportunities to learn new skills and connect with like-minded individuals. Activities such as camping and tending an allotment are not only enjoyable but also useful in a prepper context, as they help build self-sufficiency and resourcefulness. The focus is on being prepared, not necessarily expecting disaster. As one individual notes, This is not a way of life where I sit in a bunker hoping for the sky to fall." Instead, it's about having a plan and being ready, just in case. Ultimately, prepping is about taking control of one's situation and being prepared for any eventuality. articles.title: Microsoft's Quantum Computing Platform Faces Criticism
articles.summary: Microsoft is pushing forward with its Majorana 2 platform despite criticism from quantum physics experts.
articles.content: Microsoft has been pushing forward with its ambitious Majorana 2 platform, despite facing criticism from experts in the quantum physics community. The company's scientists claim that their "topological qubits are powered by an enigmatic subatomic particle, but some have questioned the validity of this assertion. In a move to validate their claims, Microsoft has opened a new lab at the University of Maryland and partnered with the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) to conduct rigorous testing of their hardware. The partnership is seen as a major boost for Microsoft's quantum computing program, which aims to develop a scalable, fault-tolerant quantum computer by 2029 - three years ahead of its previously announced target of 2033. Microsoft's confidence in achieving this goal is based on research suggesting that Majorana 2 represents a significant breakthrough in the field of quantum computing. Scientists first made headlines when they claimed to have created a new type of qubit, known as the topological qubit, which was published in a study in February 2025. Theoretical physicists have long believed that topological quantum field theory, or TQFT, holds a secret to creating ultra-resilient qubits. In this framework, physical observables are not dependent on local geometry but rather on the global topology of space-time. This property makes TQFT an attractive concept for hardware developers, as it could enable the creation of qubits that can withstand disturbances such as atmospheric noise and perturbations. Unlike conventional modalities like superconducting qubits, which are easily disrupted. Microsoft has been exploring the potential of TQFT in quantum computing by building a platform named after theoretical physicist Ettore Majorana, who hypothesized the existence of particles that act as their own antiparticles back in 1937. The company's internal data suggests that its Majorana 2 platform creates qubits with a remarkably long lifespan, ranging from 20 seconds to a minute. This is a significant improvement over conventional qubits, which typically last only microseconds. However, Microsoft has faced criticism and controversy surrounding the use of TQFT in quantum computing. A study published in Nature Reviews Materials in 2018 by Roman Lutchyn and his team claimed to have observed evidence of Majorana zero modes, but several physicists raised objections when reviewing the data in 2019. The study was eventually retracted in 2021 after the authors conceded that their methodology may have been flawed, leading to allegations of data trimming, confirmation bias, and misidentifying trivial electrical noise as exotic physics. The controversy surrounding Microsoft's quantum computing technology has persisted, with many experts questioning its feasibility. Critics have pointed out that Microsoft researchers didn't actually operate a working qubit in their experiments, instead tracking how long an electron state remained undisturbed before being disrupted by a stray charge. This approach has been likened to measuring the reliability of a qubit by observing its parity state, which is not a direct or meaningful way to assess a qubit's functionality. Some have compared Microsoft's early efforts in quantum computing to the Wright brothers' initial airplane trials, noting that these pioneering endeavors often face skepticism and criticism from outsiders. A key figure in the field has expressed his own reservations about the hype surrounding nascent quantum computing technologies like Majorana, suggesting that practical applications are more important than breakthroughs themselves. The evaluation process for Microsoft's Majorana 2 platform will be a rigorous one, as DARPA assesses its claims of achieving fault-tolerant quantum computing. This assessment involves building the device from scratch, an engineering feat that requires precision and attention to detail, according to Zulfi Alam, corporate vice president of Azure Quantum at Microsoft. The secret sauce is that we build our devices atom by atom, and that reduces disorder dramatically," Alam explained, highlighting a key aspect of Majorana 2's design. However, critics have raised questions about the practical applications of topological qubits, which are central to Microsoft's claims. DARPA has taken notice of these concerns and is evaluating Majorana 2 as part of its Quantum Benchmarking Initiative, aiming to determine whether an industrially useful quantum computer can be built by 2033. As part of this initiative, a team from the University of Maryland will conduct hands-on research at Microsoft's newly established quantum computing lab on campus. Microsoft's quantum computing technology has been put under scrutiny by DARPA, but what if it proves to be a game-changer? The Majorana 2 platform is being assessed for its ability to store quantum information, a crucial aspect of quantum computing. According to Alam, Microsoft is eager to face the challenge and prove its capabilities at the forefront of quantum research. DARPA has a team of engineers operating the machine at the University of Maryland, carefully examining every detail of the results. These engineers are responsible for reviewing massive data dumps every six months, providing DARPA with regular updates on Microsoft's progress. Microsoft's claims about Majorana 2 indicate that it can solve some of quantum computing's biggest challenges. One of these challenges is designing reliable qubits, a task considered to be the greatest hurdle in developing practical quantum computers. To tackle problems at the edges of cryptography, chemistry, and physics, millions of qubits are needed, but scaling current systems poses significant infrastructure issues. Hardware limitations, such as the need for dedicated analog microwave lines for each physical qubit, make it difficult to scale up existing systems like those developed by IBM and Google. However, if Majorana 2 works as claimed, these hardware bottlenecks would be resolved, as its qubits can be controlled digitally via an integrated processor core that requires only a few connecting wires. A revolutionary quantum computing platform developed by Microsoft is being assessed by DARPA, a US defense agency responsible for pushing technological boundaries. The Majorana 2 technology claims to produce qubits exponentially more reliable than those on other platforms, which in turn could significantly reduce the number of error-correcting qubits needed for a stable system. This reduction would have far-reaching implications, particularly for complex encryption algorithms that are currently considered unbreakable by classical computers. However, if a sufficiently powerful quantum system were to crack these codes, it's hypothesized that the time required to do so could be reduced from years to mere months or even hours. The potential impact of Majorana 2 on the field of quantum computing is substantial, with some experts suggesting that it could revolutionize the way complex problems are approached. If verified, this technology would likely shorten the timelines for achieving quantum advantage in various fields of study by several years. According to an expert not directly involved in the research, if Microsoft's Majorana 2 platform truly solves error correction issues, the current deadline of 2035 for achieving a significant breakthrough in quantum computing may no longer be credible. This would mean that the field is progressing faster than anticipated, with potentially profound implications for future technological advancements. A breakthrough of this kind would indeed mark a significant turning point in the development of quantum computing, and its consequences could be far-reaching, leading to a major shift in how we approach complex problems and solve them using advanced technologies. articles.title: Atlassian's market value reaches $35 billion
articles.summary: Atlassian's CEO Mike Cannon-Brookes attributes his company's success to unlikely events rather than deliberate strategy.
articles.content: Atlassian's market value has skyrocketed to $35 billion, with revenue projected at an annual rate of $8 billion and over 13,000 employees worldwide. The company's CEO, Mike Cannon-Brookes, boasts a personal fortune of $10 billion due in part to the fact that venture capital funding never diluted his ownership stake during Atlassian's early days. Cannon-Brookes attributes the company's origins to a series of unlikely events rather than any deliberate strategy. Speaking candidly at Web Summit in Lisbon, he cautioned against emulating Atlassian's path: "Don't copy our story... It's not very good; it's not." He emphasized that his company's success is not a model for others. Cannon-Brookes and co-founder Scott Farquhar share a common educational background, having taken the same course at the University of New South Wales. Initially, they had both applied only for scholarships to fund their studies, as neither could afford the tuition fees on their own. When Cannon-Brookes originally pursued his interest in architecture, he found it was financially unviable. As a result, he applied for various scholarships to support his education, and ultimately took up a course that combined computer studies and finance due to its availability of funding. Farquhar had initially been accepted into the Australian Defense Force Academy but received no letter confirming his place. Assuming he had been rejected, he then secured the same scholarship that Cannon-Brookes was awarded: $15,000 per year, tax-free, to study a course that blended computer science and finance. The work-experience placement that came with Cannon-Brookes' course was a six-month stint at companies in Wisconsin, where he and his classmates would install Windows on office desktop computers. It was an era when updating operating software meant physically inserting a CD into the machine, a process that likely left many users frustrated. Cannon-Brookes recalled one of his placements, where his classmate Scott was tasked with upgrading Microsoft Windows 95 to Windows 98 for months on end. He would often say it was the most boring thing he'd ever done, Cannon-Brookes said. The monotony of corporate life was a common sentiment among the two classmates, who shared their dissatisfaction with the experience. Cannon-Brookes had already gained some entrepreneurial experience by selling his small startup, The Bookmark Box, to Blink.com, an early web search tool company. The early days of Atlassian were marked by experimentation and innovation as its founders sought to create a more efficient tool for customer support teams. Initially, they aimed to work closely with these teams but soon grew dissatisfied with their existing bug-tracking software. In response, they took matters into their own hands and developed Jira, the company's flagship project management and issue tracking tool that would become synonymous with Atlassian's brand. The decision was driven by a desire for better solutions, and it paid off in the long run. At the time, online transactions were still in their infancy, with most software sales relying on physical DVDs due to limited internet bandwidth. To process payments, Atlassian had a cumbersome system involving a downloadable Word document that customers would print and fax back to the company, where orders would be manually entered into a PC. The founders' bold predictions about the potential of online software distribution and open-source models proved remarkably prescient, with both ideas revolutionizing the industry at an unprecedented scale. articles.summary: Violence erupted ahead of Thursday's Europa League match between Levski Sofia and Olympique Marseille, resulting in five Bulgarian fans being taken to hospital.
articles.content: Violence erupted ahead of Thursday's Europa League match between Levski Sofia and Olympique Marseille, resulting in five Bulgarian fans being taken to hospital. The clashes occurred at the Stade Vélodrome, where tensions had been building in the lead-up to the game. Local media reported that a disturbing number of Levski fans were spotted giving Nazi salutes as the trouble began. As the violence escalated, footage shared widely on social media showed one Levski supporter performing a Nazi salute towards the Marseille fans before the confrontation turned ugly. Eyewitness accounts suggest multiple Bulgarian fans repeated this gesture in the moments leading up to the skirmish. The French and Bulgarian presidents have condemned the actions of their respective home fans, with Emmanuel Macron describing the incidents as "acts of violence targeting Bulgarian fans" in the strongest possible terms. The clashes between fans of Levski Sofia and Marseille have left several people injured, including some who were taken to hospital for treatment. In a statement on Facebook, a senior official expressed concern about the safety of away team supporters, saying that everyone should be able to enjoy the game without fear of violence. She highlighted the importance of maintaining an atmosphere of respect and inclusivity during international matches. The official's words come as several hundred Marseille fans suddenly left their stand around 10 minutes before kickoff. Eyewitnesses described how these fans then appeared to pursue a group of Levski supporters, breaching the designated area for away teams. The situation quickly escalated into a physical confrontation, with some Marseille fans wearing face coverings. An AFP journalist at the scene reported on the fighting that broke out among the crowds. Five people were taken to hospital as a result of the clashes, suffering from injuries including eye trauma and head wounds. Several others received treatment for various minor wounds before being released. According to reports from the police prefecture in Marseille, all those hurt were Bulgarian fans. Police and security personnel struggled to contain the escalating tensions between Levski Sofia and Marseille fans outside the Stade Vélodrome before Thursday's Europa League game. The situation took a turn for the worse as groups of opposing supporters clashed, resulting in five people being hospitalised. Iotova, the Bulgarian sports minister, was quick to condemn the violence, issuing a strongly-worded statement on social media. She called out the far-right elements allegedly involved, saying They have no place in our stadiums! The French authorities are now under pressure to investigate the circumstances surrounding the attacks and hold those responsible accountable. Security personnel eventually managed to restore order as the game got underway, but not before another flare-up between fans during half-time. The match itself ended with a 1-0 victory for Marseille. articles.title: Human History Redefined by Urine Discovery
articles.summary: A revolutionary discovery has been unearthed that could redefine our understanding of human history's most pivotal moments.
articles.content: A revolutionary discovery has been unearthed that could redefine our understanding of human history's most pivotal moments. At its heart lies a substance so ordinary it's often overlooked, urine. For centuries, alchemists in medieval Europe were fixated on the elusive "Philosopher's Stone, believing it held the key to transmutation. However, their pursuit was ultimately doomed by the fundamental flaws in their approach. A closer examination of human history reveals that a more transformative substance has been quietly influencing our progress all along, one that has left an indelible mark on the course of civilisation. The story begins with a rather surprising candidate: urine. The development of civilisation itself was built upon the mastery of chemistry, and it's here that we find the first crucial step in human advancement. Fire, the first chemical reaction we learned to control, played a vital role in keeping us warm, cooking our food, and smelting ores, laying the groundwork for our modern world. Leatherwork played a crucial role in human survival across the globe. Early humans harnessed the power of urine to obtain urea, which bacteria could break down into ammonia, providing a readily available base that could soften organic matter and tan hides with ease. This fundamental discovery enabled every civilization, from those in the Americas to Europe, Africa, and Asia, to rely heavily on leatherwork for essential needs like clothing, structures, industry, and commerce. Even cultures that bypassed the bronze age or didn't develop it at all found leatherwork indispensable. The significance of urine's contribution to human progress extended far beyond its initial application in leatherwork. It also played a pivotal role in maintaining civilization as we know it today. In ancient Rome, laundries utilized urine to keep togas looking their whitest best, prompting Emperor Vespasian to impose a tax on draining urinals, with part of the revenue used to construct the iconic Colosseum. The value of urine's properties soon seeped into the realm of chemical science. In Alexandria, Egypt, artisans recognized its worth and incorporated it into their craft, laying the groundwork for alchemy's emergence. The use of water as a substitute for human urine in chemical reactions has become more widely accepted today. This shift in understanding is a result of advances in chemistry that have made it possible to replicate the desired effects without relying on the potentially hazardous and unreliable substance. As civilizations continued to develop, so did the widespread application of urine in various industries. In addition to its use in laundry and leatherwork, urine was also utilized in the production of gunpowder. This potent explosive had a significant impact on warfare, changing the dynamics of battlefields around the world. The key component of gunpowder is saltpetre, or potassium nitrate, which was often extracted from nitre beds - large heaps of manure mixed with potash and mortar, all moistened with urine. This method allowed for the collection of nitrates, a crucial element in the production process. The use of urine in the gunpowder industry was not limited to any particular region or time period. It remained a common practice from Europe to Japan, persisting well into the 19th century. Even during significant conflicts like the US Civil War, urine played a role in maintaining the functionality of firearms. By the 17th century, alchemy had become a prominent pursuit among some individuals, including Hennig Brand in Hamburg. His search for the philosopher's stone involved collecting large quantities of fermented urine, which he used to attempt to unlock its secrets. The concentrated urine at the center of Brand's experiment began to emit a faint glow, leaving him in utter astonishment. After years of secrecy, Brand finally shared his discovery with the world by selling the recipe to a friend, marking a significant turning point in the history of chemistry. This breakthrough paved the way for future discoveries and advancements in the field. The revelation sparked widespread interest and curiosity among scientists and scholars. The experiment was not an illusion or a magic trick, but rather a remarkable achievement that isolated phosphorus, a fundamental chemical element discovered in modern times. This discovery had far-reaching implications and marked a significant milestone in the history of science. Phosphorus is still widely used today in various applications, from lighting to fertilizers. Urine continues to play a vital role in medicine, serving as a rich source of biomarkers for diagnostic tests and providing essential substances like human chorionic gonadotropin and follicle-stimulating hormone for fertility treatment. As the ancient Roman Emperor Vespasian aptly noted, money doesn't stink," echoing the valuable contributions that urine has made to human progress. articles.title: Ancient Scrolls Unearthed in Egypt in 1827
articles.summary: A treasure trove of ancient scrolls was unearthed in Egypt in 1827 by a graverobber who initially considered leaving them behind.
articles.content: In a remarkable archaeological discovery, a treasure trove of ancient scrolls was unearthed in Egypt in 1827 by a graverobber who initially considered leaving them behind. The raider's decision to take the documents to market proved to be a shrewd one, as they were soon acquired by Jean d'Anastasy, a discerning buyer with an eye for valuable artifacts. D'Anastasy's purchase would go on to have far-reaching implications, not only for the field of Egyptology but also for our understanding of ancient alchemy. As it turns out, one of the scrolls contained a recipe for a potent concoction that involved mixing lime and sulfur powder with vinegar or the urine of a small child. The instructions for this mysterious brew were eerily reminiscent of modern-day laboratory procedures. The scroll's author, unknown to us today, was clearly well-versed in the principles of chemistry, even if they didn't have a name for it at the time. This early example of alchemical experimentation highlights the ingenuity and resourcefulness of ancient practitioners. The Leiden Papyrus X, as this document has come to be known, is a testament to the sophistication and curiosity of our ancestors. Dating back to around 300 CE, its contents reveal a deep understanding of chemical processes that would not be matched for centuries to come. As we delve deeper into the world of ancient alchemy, it becomes increasingly clear that these early experimenters were driven by a desire to unlock the secrets of nature. The discovery of Leiden Papyrus X has shed new light on the evolution of chemistry and our understanding of the ancient world. But what other secrets lie hidden in the dusty recesses of history, waiting to be uncovered? A grain merchant turned diplomat, Constantine d'Anastasy's life was marked by intrigue and opportunism. Born in Greece to a family that had seen its fortunes rise and fall during the Napoleonic Wars, he leveraged his connections to establish himself in Alexandria. D'Anastasy's business dealings were not limited to trading; he also ran a clandestine operation, acquiring relics from Ancient Egypt and selling them to European collectors. His network extended from the British Museum in London to the Louvre in Paris, where he would procure statues, rings, and jewels for wealthy patrons. Among his most notable acquisitions was a pair of sphinxes that now adorn the banks of the Neva River in St Petersburg. D'Anastasy's entrepreneurial spirit knew no bounds as he exploited opportunities wherever they arose. He soon discovered that the papers he had acquired held significant value, and he quickly made arrangements to transport them back to Europe for sale. Some were destined for Stockholm, while others would find a home at Leiden University in the Netherlands. A remarkable discovery was made among the Leiden collection: an ancient papyrus scroll containing recipes for creating seemingly magical riches. Written in Greek around 300 CE, this alchemy book is now recognized as the oldest surviving text of its kind. In ancient alchemy texts, readers are given detailed instructions on how to create gold-like effects using common household items and gardening supplies. Some of these recipes may seem far-fetched or even laughable today, but they actually work, albeit with some modern shortcuts. Among the various concoctions described in The Age of Alchemy is a recipe for creating "sulfur water, considered one of the greatest secrets in alchemy. This mixture involves combining sulfur and lime, which can be found in most hardware stores, along with vinegar as an alternative to a child's urine - a surprising ingredient that was once used. When heated for an hour, the resulting substance is a reddish-brown goop that smells eerily like rotten eggs. This unappealing outcome is actually calcium polysulfides, also known as lime sulfur, which has been repurposed in modern times as a pest control agent due to its strong alkali properties. However, in ancient alchemy, this concoction was believed to be the key to creating gold-like effects on metal objects. By submerging coins, nails, or paperclips into the sulfur water", they would supposedly gain a thin, yellowish film coating that mimicked the appearance of gold. While it's clear that these ancient alchemists were not actually producing solid gold, their recipes demonstrate an understanding of chemical reactions and the manipulation of materials to achieve specific effects. The Leiden Papyrus X is often seen as an ancient guide for tricksters, but its true significance goes beyond mere deception. Its recipes demonstrate a surprising understanding of chemical reactions and material manipulation, hinting at a more sophisticated knowledge than initially meets the eye. While it may seem like these alchemists were merely trying to swindle their customers, closer examination reveals a more nuanced picture. The document's authorship remains unknown, but the workshop where this text was created 1,700 years ago would have been a hub of activity, with individuals experimenting and innovating in various fields. Chemistry as we know it today did not emerge overnight, nor can it be attributed to a single person or era; instead, it developed gradually over time through the contributions of many cultures and civilizations. The transformation from primitive understanding to modern chemistry was a gradual process that spanned millennia. This journey was facilitated by countless individuals who contributed to the development of chemistry, often without receiving due recognition for their efforts. A comprehensive history of alchemy would be incomplete if it were to focus solely on Western traditions, which have been extensively studied and documented. In contrast, this book takes a more inclusive approach, delving into the development of chemistry in various cultures around the world, including those in the Islamic world, China, India, and the Americas. The author's journey to craft an engaging narrative is reflected in their exploration of old roads and interaction with researchers pushing the boundaries of new knowledge. This approach has yielded a story that not only chronicles scientific progress but also celebrates its significance in everyday life, often revealing unexpected connections between past and present. Chemistry plays a ubiquitous role, influencing various aspects of our lives, and it's remarkable how this field is characterized by both human imperfections and noble endeavors. According to officials, the talks set for this Friday in Islamabad will focus on recent developments in the region, including attacks by Yemen's Houthi rebels against Saudi Arabia. This concern is at the forefront of discussions between the three nations, with a particular emphasis on countering threats from external forces. Security officials have confirmed that delegations from Turkey and Saudi Arabia are already arriving in Pakistan's capital to participate in the talks. The presence of these representatives underscores the importance placed by the countries on strengthening their defense ties. Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan has formally given his approval for the agreement, marking the completion of the ratification process in Turkey. This move comes after Turkish lawmakers approved the pact earlier this month, despite some opposition from parties concerned about potential involvement in regional conflicts. The agreement's defensive nature has been emphasized by Pakistani officials, who insist it is not directed against any country, including Iran. This stance aims to alleviate concerns that the trilateral alliance might escalate regional tensions or get entangled in existing conflicts. According to sources, senior officials from Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkey will convene to explore ways of bolstering their strategic security cooperation. Discussions are expected to cover a range of topics, including intelligence sharing, military collaboration, and enhancing ties between defense industries. Pakistan's Defense Minister Khawaja Muhammad Asif has underscored the country's commitment to defending its allies against external threats, stating that it will utilize all available means to safeguard Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks. This pledge reflects Pakistan's willingness to play a more active role in regional security arrangements. The meeting of the Strategic, Political and Defense Committee is part of the Joint Mecca Defense Agreement, signed in August by leaders from the three participating countries. The pact aims to foster greater cooperation on defense matters among its signatories, with the ultimate goal of strengthening regional stability. The trilateral defense pact between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkey is set to take a significant step forward as the three countries prepare to meet in Islamabad. In preparation for the high-profile gathering, local authorities have declared a holiday in the capital city to minimize public movement and facilitate security measures. Road diversions are being implemented by Islamabad traffic police, with motorists advised to use alternative routes to accommodate the arrival of foreign delegations. This logistical effort is aimed at ensuring the smooth flow of traffic during the meeting, which will bring together representatives from all three signatory countries. The pact's implementation is expected to strengthen regional stability through enhanced cooperation on defense matters among its member states. With a 10-year commitment and provision for a three-month notice period before withdrawal, the agreement provides a framework for sustained collaboration between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkey. articles.title: Quantum Mechanics Breakthrough: Paraparticles Observed in Complex System
articles.summary: A team of scientists has made a groundbreaking discovery in the field of quantum mechanics by observing particles known as paraparticles in a complex system.
articles.content: A team of scientists has made a groundbreaking discovery in the field of quantum mechanics by observing particles known as paraparticles in a complex system. The experiment involved a quantum simulator containing 16 qubits, which is a significant milestone in understanding these elusive particles that were thought to be impossible to detect. Paraparticles are classified based on their behavior when they swap places and how many can share the same quantum state simultaneously. This characteristic sets them apart from bosons and fermions, which have distinct properties. The existence of paraparticles was first proposed in the 1950s, but it seemed that distinguishing them from other particles would be a major challenge, limiting our understanding of the quantum world. Physicists have made a significant breakthrough in observing particles not seen before in experiments. The team used a quantum simulator to find signs of paraparticles, as suggested by mathematical work from earlier years. A total of 16 qubits were employed, each consisting of tiny superconducting circuits arranged in a grid-like pattern. These qubits were paired using electromagnetic interactions, effectively creating rungs on a ladder that behaved like paraparticles. The researchers conducted three tests to confirm the emergence of paraparticles: swapping them, making them collide, and studying how they grouped together. Each test was carefully designed to observe distinct properties of these novel particles. A year's worth of effort went into calibrating and controlling the qubits to produce reliable results. The team's findings are significant because they demonstrate that paraparticles are not purely theoretical concepts but can be experimentally observed, providing a proof of concept for further research. The team's experiment uses qubits' unique properties as building blocks to create paraparticles, a concept previously thought purely theoretical. This approach differs significantly from conventional computer simulations, where code is written in an abstract form without any physical presence, according to Hays. The team aims to replicate the complexity of real-world systems by manipulating these particles in various geometrical configurations. The researchers plan to explore interactions between paraparticles and more intricate arrangements, which could shed light on the many open questions surrounding these entities, as noted by Wang. articles.content: A thrilling conclusion to a college basketball game unfolded at Michelob Ultra Arena on Thursday night, as No. 25 Louisville edged out No. 13 St. John's in a heart-stopping 93-90 win. The victory marked Rick Pitino's team's first loss of the season and was all the more dramatic given the controversy that had surrounded the game. The win capped off an incredible comeback by the Cardinals, who trailed by as many as 18 points at one stage in the second half but managed to fight back to secure the narrow victory. Louisville's Adrian Wooley proved to be the hero of the night, sinking a crucial three-pointer from the left corner on a broken play that sealed the win for his team. The shot was described by Cardinals coach Pat Kelsey as one that Wooley will "tell his grandkids about in years to come. Meanwhile, Rick Pitino attributed the loss to a combination of good defense and a little bit of luck, noting that Wooley's shot was lucky." Despite their valiant efforts, St. John's ultimately came up short, with Louisville scoring 57 points in the first half alone - the most points allowed by Pitino's team since he took over as coach. The Red Storm's largest halftime deficit under Pitino's leadership was a stark reminder of just how dominant the Cardinals had been. The win marked Louisville's second consecutive victory against a ranked opponent, and it sets them up nicely for their next game against No. 9 Tennessee on Friday night. With the opportunity to claim the Players Era 16 title hanging in the balance, the Cardinals will be looking to build on this momentum as they take on the Volunteers. As for St. John's, the loss was a tough pill to swallow after such a promising start to the season. With their first defeat of the year now behind them, Pitino and his team will be eager to bounce back and get back on track in their next game. The drama that unfolded at Michelob Ultra Arena on Thursday night has left fans and pundits alike buzzing with excitement.
